title: One-point distribution of the geodesic in directed last passage percolation: the generalized Cauchy identity (Lemma 2.9)
author: Zhipeng Liu
work: One-point distribution of the geodesic in directed last passage percolation
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the generalized Cauchy identity that the paper isolates as the algebraic engine of its finite-time formula, and its 202-line proof is the author’s own, not a citation and not a rerun of the classical Cauchy determinant identity. With the classical Cauchy determinant formula and elementary determinant expansion supplied as prerequisites, the author must still set up the auxiliary sums C_{p,q} of signed cofactors, evaluate them by converting the double sum into a contour integral and reading off residues (carried out in full for C_{-1,2}), tabulate the six C_{p,q} values used later, expand the bordered determinant carrying the u-linear and y_b/x_a^2 terms into a sum over index pairs (a,b), and reassemble everything into the identity eq:sum_identity_01, whose u^2 coefficient must cancel and whose remaining terms must equal (1-rz)^{N-2}(H(X;Y) + rz prod_i(y_i/x_i) H(Y;X)) det[1/(y_j-x_i)]. The author himself records that the computation is tedious while its strategy is quite straightforward, that the auxiliary identities are listed without proofs because they are analogous to the one shown, and that the last step is a careful but straightforward calculation; he also states that this identity is much more complicated than the simpler Lemma 5.5 of Baik-Liu to which the same residue strategy was applied. That combination - a multi-parameter determinant identity with a genuinely new right-hand side, verified term by term through auxiliary residue evaluations that are not available off the shelf - is beyond a routine qualifying-exercise determinant manipulation, while remaining below the top of the scale because each individual step is a standard residue/expansion computation with no new concept introduced.
